findings.title: Structured-only reads cannot authorize subsequent mutations
findings.why_it_matters: With the documented `--payload structured` mode, a successful `tb_content` returns its hash to the caller but every subsequent read-gated write, edit or delete is rejected as if the file had never been read. `served_hash` reads only the text content block, which this mode deliberately omits, so the read ledger is never populated. Extracting the hash from structured content first, with a text fallback, makes the gate independent of the selected response representation.
findings.suggested_fix: Read the content hash from `structured_content` when present, otherwise parse the text block; add read-then-mutate integration coverage for both, text and structured payload modes.
evidence: tb-mcp-rs/src/lib.rs:4138-4140: PayloadMode::Structured sets only `response.structured_content`; tb_content records a read only when served_hash returns Some at lines 1184-1186.
tb-mcp-rs/src/gate.rs:65-70 rejects a mutation without a recorded prior read.

findings.title: Content continuation offsets cannot be supplied back
findings.why_it_matters: A caller that requests a bounded `tb_content` window receives `next_offset` but cannot retrieve the remaining text in another bounded call: the request schema has no offset field and rejects unknown fields. Repeating the call returns the same prefix; dropping the limit returns the entire file and defeats bounded retrieval. Accepting a character offset and applying it when constructing the window makes the advertised continuation usable.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an optional character offset to ContentArguments, slice from that offset, and return a nullable next_offset only while text remains; cover multi-page Unicode content and the final page.
evidence: tb-mcp-rs/src/lib.rs:569-582 declares only repo, path and max_chars with `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`; lines 4312-4317 always take the first `max` characters.
tb-mcp-rs/tests/budgets.rs:64-75 checks the first window and advertised continuation, but not consuming it.

findings.title: Candidate scans default to unbounded full-detail replies
findings.why_it_matters: An agent calling `tb_candidates` without optional arguments receives full candidate detail for the entire workspace; the review's live call produced roughly 1.4 MB in one response. This needlessly consumes client context and can eventually exceed the adapter's 16 MiB engine-frame limit, making the read fail as the workspace grows. Pagination exists but is opt-in, and concise discovery strips the parameter descriptions; a bounded default with explicit continuation makes the ordinary call safe without hiding further results.
findings.suggested_fix: Default the MCP candidate call to a bounded page such as 50 files, expose total/offset/nullable next_offset in the candidate response schema, and document an explicit full scan or page through the complete set. Preserve engine compatibility deliberately if its unbounded wire contract must remain unchanged.
evidence: tb-engine/crates/tb-engine/src/serve.rs:2454-2459: summary defaults to full and an absent limit returns every scanned file; dispatch passes the optional limit unchanged at lines 12589-12595.
tb-engine/crates/tb-engine/src/wire.rs:1468-1472 uses `take(limit.unwrap_or(usize::MAX))`; tb-mcp-rs/src/lib.rs:2438-2446 forwards a limit only if supplied.
tb-mcp-rs/src/lib.rs:3402-3414 strips parameter descriptions from the default concise profile; the parent observed a roughly 1.4 MB response to the default live call.
